Tell Me What You See.quote: Yeah, I I'm definitely wanting to build around it. We'll go build around Beyond Tell me what you see.
Tell Me What You See.gist: A dilemma build-around that returns to hand to be replayed. The opponent's choice (you draw, or they lose 4 and you surveil) is decent either way.
Tell Me What You See.note: Caption 'build around Beyond' = 'build around B on'. The other host first said 'probably like a builder around B' (2:19:38).

Temporal Anomaly.quote: I think the anomaly lands, the ones that sack and make a planet are just all B minuses. >> Yeah, agreed.
Temporal Anomaly.gist: Utility lands that sacrifice for a spell-like effect and replace themselves with a Planet; extra good in Strange New Worlds.
Temporal Anomaly.note: Group grade for the five Anomaly lands (Subspace Anomaly read in full, the others described by LSV); earlier LSV said 'C plus all of them, maybe even B minus'. Green one: 3G mill four, take a permanent.

Temporal Conqueror.quote: >> But yeah, this this looks like a C++ to me. This looks like one of the top comments.
Temporal Conqueror.gist: Fills the graveyard and nearly always returns a land: card advantage on fine stats.
Temporal Conqueror.note: Caption 'C++' read as C+; 'top comments' = top commons.

Tenacious Drone.quote: Yeah, this looks great. This looks like another C++ to me. Like, I'll be really happy playing this card in pretty much any black deck
Tenacious Drone.gist: A two-for-one artifact two-drop that is good in any black deck, especially the artifact and sacrifice decks.

Test of Conviction.quote: Yeah, I like B minus. I think like it's a sorcery, so you're not tricking them. But >> that's true. >> Yeah, I like B minus for test of conviction.
Test of Conviction.gist: Mostly a two-mana sorcery that puts a counter on each creature; good in go-wide or counters decks, and the draw mode is for when you're losing.
Test of Conviction.note: Other host first said 'this would probably play like a B' if going wide or caring about counters (1:01:34, 1:02:30), then accepted the sorcery-speed point ('that's true').

Test of Courage.quote: >> it does look cool. I would give it a rare these days buildaround or sorry >> sideboard. >> Yeah, >> this looks like a sideboard beam.
Test of Courage.gist: Mainly a sideboard card (cheap artifact/enchantment removal or graveyard hate), though maindecking it wouldn't be a disaster.
Test of Courage.note: Graded as 'sideboard' with no clear letter; 'sideboard beam' might be a mis-caption of 'sideboard B'.

Test of Identity.quote: I think if you had three or four Klingons, I would probably play this card. Otherwise, I would usually avoid it. So, that probably makes it about a D. >> Yeah, D.
Test of Identity.gist: Strong Klingon combat trick but the Tormenting Voice mode is weak; only with several Klingons.

Test of Loyalty.quote: I I like C for test of loyalty. Just it looks totally solid. >> I do too. Either way, you're getting a card out of it.
Test of Loyalty.gist: Either cycles while exiling a graveyard card or acts as Raise Dead; either way you get a card.

Test of Priorities.quote: I like C++ for for a test of priorities. >> That's exactly where I put it.
Test of Priorities.gist: Instant-speed surveil 2 plus a draw earns it a deck slot, and it can also save a creature you have invested in.
Test of Priorities.note: Caption 'C++' read as C+. Both agreed.

The Doctor, EMH.quote: Yeah, this looks like a buildaround B. Like this looks like the this looks like the five drop you'd want in green white.
The Doctor, EMH.gist: Lots of stats, and it multiplies counters when you already have countered creatures; the five-drop a green-white counters deck wants.
The Doctor, EMH.note: Other host agrees: 'Totally. Especially if you've built around it in any capacity.'

The Duras Sisters.quote: Two mana 32 that dies into a two-1. That's just an easy two for one for two mana. I like B for Duras Sisters.
The Duras Sisters.gist: A two-mana 3/2 that dies into a hasty 2/1 is an easy two-for-one, playable in most decks heavy in black or red.

The Measure of a Man.quote: What do you want to give this like C plus? >> I want to give it like a C. >> Yeah,
The Measure of a Man.gist: Not real removal: it holds a creature off for about two turns, plus a clue and a little life; flexible but the creature comes back.
The Measure of a Man.note: One host floats C+, the other says C, answered 'Yeah' before moving on. Read as settled at C; if not, it would be C/C+.

The Naked Time.quote: This looks like a D. >> Can I just say F? >> You could say F. Sure. ... I think a D is probably fine, but it's closer to an F. D minus. Sure.
The Naked Time.gist: Only borrows a land for two turns and gives about one +1/+1 counter; some landfall tricks in RG.
The Naked Time.note: Started at D, Marshall suggested F, settled on D-.

The Traveler.quote: you would like to get it to a 33. So yes, C++ for the Traveler. Looks solid. Doesn't look amazing.
The Traveler.gist: A two-mana 2/3 reach vigilance at baseline that grows a bit with differently named lands; fine in most blue-green decks without extra work.
The Traveler.note: Also 'I think it looks like a C plus to me' (0:44:44). Caption 'C++' read as C+. Other host: 'that's exactly how I see it.'

There's Coffee in that Nebula.quote: I I would go C minus on there's coffee in that nebula and then see see if be me up becomes a thing.
There's Coffee in that Nebula.gist: A weak two-mana card-selection spell; Beam me up needs good cheap ETB creatures, so the C- is a hopeful grade.
There's Coffee in that Nebula.note: They call C- 'a hopeful grade' and say 'right now this card is a D'. Also 'this might actually be a buildaround in some strange way', but the grade isn't given as build-around.

Those Old Scientists.quote: I would give it a D minus. >> Yeah, I like that. >> It's just too slow.
Those Old Scientists.gist: Card-neutral and too slow. The chapter III shuffle only matters in very long games.

Transporter Malfunction.quote: >> Yeah, I like B+ for transfer function. >> B+ excellent removal.
Transporter Malfunction.gist: Two mana for 3 damage to any target is great; the expensive beam-me-up is pure gravy.

Tricorder.quote: I don't really like it in a lot of the other archetypes. So, I'm still going to give this like probably like a C C minus or so.
Tricorder.gist: Like the underrated S.H.I.E.L.D. spy kit; good in artifact (Borg) decks, less so elsewhere.
Tricorder.note: Said 'like a C, C minus or so'; recorded the last letter. Marshall: 'Maybe it's better.' Captioned 'triquarter'.

Type-2 Phaser.quote: >> I like two phaser at like a C++. I think this card is going to be good in the right deck.
Type-2 Phaser.gist: Stun on entry plus +3/+0; equip 3 is costly but it shines with BW 1/1 tokens.

U.S.S. Cerritos, Following Up.quote: so I would just give it a B. I think USS Cerritos is going to play well.
U.S.S. Cerritos, Following Up.gist: Two 1/1 tokens plus a 4/4 flyer: lots of board presence; a similar card was good before.

U.S.S. Excelsior, Cutting Edge.quote: I I would give us USS USS Excelsier B minus. I think it's going to be just a pretty good card. >> I agree.
U.S.S. Excelsior, Cutting Edge.gist: A mediocre sorcery-speed kill on a tapped creature that can later become a 4/4 flyer; they bet Spacecraft have enough payoffs.

U.S.S. Voyager, Lone Wanderer.quote: I think this is like a B-level card in blue, green, and red green. ... maybe a C- level card in black green, and probably like a D or an F in white green.
U.S.S. Voyager, Lone Wanderer.gist: Puts two lands into play for double landfall; great in UG and RG, poor elsewhere.
U.S.S. Voyager, Lone Wanderer.note: Grades split by archetype, no overall grade: B in UG and RG, C- in BG, D or F in GW. Grade field holds the grade for its main archetypes.

Una Chin-Riley, Number One.quote: this thing's a great blocker. I like C++ for Unichin Riley.
Una Chin-Riley, Number One.gist: A 4/5 that gets you halfway to 8 power and blocks well; the exalted-like +2/+0 and first strike makes an attacker hard to block.
Una Chin-Riley, Number One.note: Captions: 'Unona Chin Riley', 'Unichin Riley'. Other host: 'I still like C++ on this. I don't know that I would quite get it to the B range' (1:30:44). 'C++' read as C+.

Unexplored Territory.quote: So it's like a C. It's not that it's worse than evolving wilds, I think, in most decks and better in the red green deck is my guess.
Unexplored Territory.gist: Taps for colorless before cracking for a basic, so landfall decks can time the trigger; better than Evolving Wilds in RG.

V'Ger, the Intruder.quote: Okay. Um like a C plus for that. >> I would give it like a builder B. I think it's going to be good if you can cast it.
V'Ger, the Intruder.gist: A seven-mana finisher for ramp decks. The -1/-0 mode and the card draw with a look at the hand are strong if you can cast it.
V'Ger, the Intruder.note: Captions say 'Vagr'. One host said C+ (as a ramp finisher); the other said build-around B. They did not settle. build_around refers to the B.

Vash, Freelance Archaeologist.quote: Yeah, I would certainly say this is a B. I like Bash. You could put this in any black green deck and it was just going to work totally fine.
Vash, Freelance Archaeologist.gist: A three-mana 2/4 that surveils every turn and draws when cards leave the graveyard; a strong enabler that asks nothing of you.
Vash, Freelance Archaeologist.note: Other host: 'I would put Vash at like a B, maybe even a B+ for enabling plus raw power' (0:38:22), assuming black-green is powered right.

Vengeance Mission.quote: I mean, it is both sides and there are a lot of tokens. I bet this card is a build around B.
Vengeance Mission.gist: Drains whenever any creature dies. One host likes it with early tokens; the other thinks reaching seven counters asks too much.
Vengeance Mission.note: Right after, apparently the other host (no speaker mark): 'Man, I want to go build around like C++ or something ... that is just asking so much. I'm off it.' (2:29:14). Build-around B vs build-around C+, not settled.

Vexing Drone.quote: sure. Yeah, I like vexing drilling at like C minus. >> Yeah, C minus.
Vexing Drone.gist: A two-mana artifact Borg creature that taps a creature when it enters, with a little Beam me up value.

Vulcan.quote: So, these are also probably like, you know what, I I just think these are C pluses ... >> Yeah, agreed.
Vulcan.gist: Tapped gain lands that fix, slow the format and help Strange New Worlds; hosts love the art.
Vulcan.note: Group grade for the cycle of 10 Planet gain lands (Vulcan read as the example); Marshall agreed. Vulcan is the card read aloud.

Vulcan Mind-Meld.quote: It looks like a D, but there's some interesting stuff going on.
Vulcan Mind-Meld.gist: Mainly for the blue-red spells deck. Trading top cards is of unclear value, though library manipulation could break it, and it looks fun to try.

Warp Core.quote: >> I like it. Bill C, baby. ... I would just give Warp Core a C. I think it's going to fit into a decent amount of places. >> I would too.
Warp Core.gist: Finds a basic land and helps spacecraft; fits a decent number of decks.
Warp Core.note: Marshall opened with 'Bill C, baby' (probably 'build C', i.e. build-around C), then agreed with LSV's plain C.

Warp Speed.quote: Yeah, I would just give warp speed a D. It just looks like it's not doing
Warp Speed.gist: Three mana to replace itself with a land and untap lands; none of its parts is impressive.

Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior.quote: I agree with you. build around C like what what's the >> build around C that means it's like a D I mean it it could it has potential
Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior.gist: A two-mana 1/1 that is unplayable as is; it needs counters from tapping artifacts or creatures, and when it doesn't work it does nothing.
Worf, Honor-Bound Warrior.note: Captions: 'Wararf', 'warf'. One host first said 'This looks kind of like a D to me, honestly' (0:41:56); they then settled on 'build around C', which they say 'means it's like a D' outside a built-around deck. Read as D: the hosts said build-around C means D.

Xenobotanist.quote: >> Great. This is a C plus. This looks fantastic.
Xenobotanist.gist: 2-mana 1/3 any-color mana creature, great for splashy Strange New Worlds decks.

Xindi Surveyors.quote: It's pretty bad one. D for Z surveyors. ... probably a D in most decks. see in in like the really heavy landfall deck.
Xindi Surveyors.gist: 3-mana 3/2 that grows on landfall; a mediocre turn-4 play.
Xindi Surveyors.note: Also called 'C slash D': D in most decks, C in the really heavy landfall deck. Captioned 'Zindy / Z surveyors'.

Zefram Cochrane, Warp Pioneer.quote: enabler for that deck. So, I like build around B+ for Zephr Cochran.
Zefram Cochrane, Warp Pioneer.gist: A great non-artifact enabler for the artifact deck that lets you cast artifacts off the top of the library. The spacecraft bonus is a nice extra.
Zefram Cochrane, Warp Pioneer.note: Captions say 'Zephrim Cochran'. The other host agreed it works well in the artifact deck.

Zero, Incorporeal Sensate.quote: I think you're probably right. All right, we'll go B for zero and corporal sensate.
Zero, Incorporeal Sensate.gist: A lifelink 2/2 that takes a card from their hand and taxes it, like Elite Spellbinder without flying.
Zero, Incorporeal Sensate.note: One host B ('I would still give this a B', 0:34:07), the other first thought B+, then they settled on B.
